_source: AI-researched NEW DISTRICT candidates for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly promoted by the research agent. Populated by the same daily scheduled research agent as venue-suggestions.json (2026-08, at explicit user request), committed straight to master the same way (see that file's own doc comment for why). Expected to be rare: the research brief (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md) treats district suggestions as an occasional finding (a genuinely distinct, not-yet-covered high-end area within Manchester or Cheshire), not a daily quota — most days should add zero entries here. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) is the only thing that promotes an entry into the real docs/data/districts.json, behind its own pull request. Each entry mirrors docs/data/districts.json's own raw shape (name/metro/lat/lon/base/kind/accentColor/editorialDescription) so an approved entry can be copied straight in, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) stripped on promotion. `metro` must be 'manchester' or 'cheshire' only — never 'los-angeles' or a new metro (out of scope, per the user's explicit 'shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet').
_reviewWorkflow: Same as venue-suggestions.json: status starts 'pending', the review agent flips it to 'approved' (then copies fields into districts.json, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (kept here with researchNotes so it isn't re-suggested). A human's real review happens by reading/merging that PR.

suggestions.name: Nantwich
suggestions.editorialDescription: A salt town before it was anything else — 'wich' means brine — with more black-and-white Tudor timber per street than the rest of the county put together, a medieval church at its centre, and a market that's run three days a week since long before most of Cheshire's other towns had a charter.
suggestions.researchNotes: Checked the district-suggestion question fresh this run rather than assuming 'usually zero' (per this file's own 2026-09-03 correction). Nantwich is a genuinely distinct, well-known Cheshire market town roughly 15 miles south of Knutsford — the southernmost existing Cheshire district — with no overlap with any of the 20 districts currently in docs/data/districts.json. Confirmed via nantwichtowncouncil.gov.uk, greatbritishlife.co.uk and visitcheshire.com: real Grade I/II-listed Tudor, Georgian and Victorian architecture, one of the country's finest medieval parish churches (St Mary's), a three-day-a-week traditional market, a genuinely independent-heavy shopping and eating scene (Nantwich Town Council's own directory lists it explicitly as independent-led, not chain-anchored), and a well-known outdoor thermal brine pool unique to the town. This is exactly the kind of 'a local would name it without hesitation' gap this file's own review process exists to catch — it sits alongside Knutsford/Prestbury/Wilmslow in every 'best Cheshire towns' list checked, the same category of omission the user flagged for those three on 2026-09-03. Coordinates (53.067/-2.5206) are St Mary's Church, the town centre, and land well within the existing lat 53.0-53.6/lon -2.6--2.0 sanity box. accentColor (#A56A52, faded brick-clay) chosen for perceptual distinctness against every existing Cheshire accent, closest neighbours being Alderley Edge (#A66B4F) and Wilmslow (#B85C3E) — distinct from both, and Nantwich is never zoomed alongside either given the real distance between them. base (56) set in line with other recently added, not-yet-populated Cheshire towns (between Wilmslow's 55 and Knutsford's 54) rather than guessed high. No venues researched or suggested yet — same starting point every prior district promotion (Chorlton, Didsbury, Stockport (Underbanks), Heaton Moor, Macclesfield, Bramhall) has had before its own first venue pass; that's separate follow-up work for whoever picks this up next, not done here.
